step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates ThreatStack's telemetry ingestion and analytics pipeline. 1. Telemetry and CloudTrail events originate from the customer's VPC (EC2 with ThreatStack agent installed and CloudTrail) and cross over to an Apache Kafka broker (MSK). 2. For near real-time processing, Kafka streams data into an Apache Flink cluster (ThirdParty), which formats and streams GZIP JSON files into a near real-time S3 bucket. 3. For long-term data warehousing (30 days retention), Kafka streams directly to an EMR ingestion cluster, which is orchestrated and managed by an orchestration EC2 instance. The EMR ingestion cluster writes structured Apache Parquet files into a dedicated S3 bucket. 4. On the analytics and consumption side, the orchestration EC2 instance submits JAR/Spark jobs to an EMR analytics cluster. Multiple analytics tools, including Athena (SQL queries), SageMaker (ML trend analysis and anomaly detection), and the EMR analytics cluster, consume the Parquet data directly from the S3 Parquet bucket.

graph.name: ThreatStack Telemetry Ingestion and Analytics Architecture
graph.notes: Architectural breakdown of ThreatStack processing 60 billion events per day using dual path processing (near real-time GZIP JSON via Flink and 30-day Parquet warehousing via EMR) consumed by Athena, SageMaker, and EMR.

nodes.name: S3 (Parquet)

nodes.notes: Orchestration service running on EC2 that spins up security-blessed EMR clusters and submits JAR/Spark jobs.

nodes.name: Athena
nodes.notes: Amazon Athena querying Parquet data in S3 for SQL-based threat investigation.
